messages:
elena: quick sync notes from the packaging sync: i propose we go patchstream-first for onprem/airgapped upgrades. build small chunked delta bundles and run a node-local verifier sidecar that signs an activation intent. operator validates intent and enforces activation lease/rollout policy. this reduces seed size and enables fast hotpatches without forcing full-image swaps.

devin: patchstream-first sounds promising. main concerns: operator-sidecar trust boundary, signature placement, and idempotency during partial applies. do we keep verification purely local?

elena: yes, verification stays in the sidecar (node-local). sidecar has minimal privileges: verify signatures and produce a signed activation-intent containing activation_id, component_set, and range hash. operator checks policy and either approves within a lease window or rejects.

ty: what about a crash between verification and activation? if node reboots after signing but before operator reads the intent, how do we avoid double-apply or stuck states?

morgan: add a short-lived activation lease embedded in the intent. operator will only accept intents with a valid lease timestamp. sidecar persists the intent in local KV so it can replay on reboot. if replay is lost, operator falls back to full-image apply path. keep all replays idempotent.

devin: manifest change required: add component-level compat anchors and optional fallback-image pointer so operator knows when to force monolithic apply. suggestion manifest snippet: ```manifest_version: 2
components:
  - name: runtime
    hash: "sha256:..."
    compat_anchors: ["1.x", "2.3.x"]
    fallback: "oci://registry/redwood/runtime:1.3.2"
```

elena: exactly. compat_anchors let policy decide if delta is safe. fallback pointer used as backstop.

ty: streaming/transport: stream a single content-addressed tar vs chunked fragments with an index? resumability vs memory pressure tradeoff.

morgan: chunked fragments + small index is preferred. index lists chunk refs, hashes, and component mapping. sidecar/operator can fetch chunks from local media or a carrier proxy. cap concurrent rehydrate workers to avoid OOM on smaller nodes.

devin: +1. also add an offline CLI to prepare bundles for field ops: `redwood pack create-patch --manifest manifest.yaml --out patchstream.tar`

ops-bot: deploy-bot: ticket RW-ENG-1452 created for 'offline bundle CLI and operator API' assigned to @elena. ETA 2w.

elena: outstanding design items: 1) operator <-> sidecar protocol (unix socket RPC vs CRD watch) 2) rollback marker/tombstone shape 3) telemetry and forensics for airgapped environments

ty: for protocol, prefer node-local unix socket RPC for verification flows (avoids k8s auth complexity). operator continues to watch node CRD for activation status. for non-k8s installs we support a systemd sidecar + local file drop that a management process scans.

morgan: rollback marker should be a signed tombstone containing activation_id, component_set, prev_hash, reason_code, and signer. operator enforces tombstone TTL and retention policy.

devin: can we reuse existing manifest merkle/range hashing code to compute range hashes? reduces new surface area.

elena: yes reuse the merkle libs. add a helper CLI: `redwood manifest rangesum --range components/runtime` to assist ops.

ty: testing: need a simulator that models partial chunk loss, intent replay after reboot, and activation races. plus a fuzz harness for compat_anchors evaluation.

morgan: perf guidance: encourage small patches (<50MB). reserve full-image applies for major releases. consider compressing model shards independently from runtime blobs so operator isn't forced to decompress huge model files during activation.

devin: security: sidecar must enforce strict signature verification and reject unknown signers. operator maps allowed signers per cluster. add a documented key-rotation and escrow procedure for airgapped customers.

ops-bot: note: @devin added RW-SPEC-223 to vendor spec board for signer mapping and rotation flow.

elena: Decision (informal): ship patchstream-first with chunked fragments + small index. sidecar handles verification and signs activation intents. operator validates intents and controls activation via lease windows. full-image apply supported as fallback. follow-ups: 1) RFC PR for sidecar/operator API and CRD shapes (owner: @elena, due EOW) 2) offline bundle CLI + packer (owner: @devin) 3) simulator + fuzz harness (owner: @ty) 4) key-rotation and escrow doc (owner: @morgan).

morgan: ack, starting rollback marker draft.

ty: will prototype simulator with random chunk loss and activation race scenarios.

devin: stub CLI repo today, will share link.

elena: thanks everyone. i'll open the RFC PR with API sketches and manifest delta examples. ping me inline if you want constraints added. :thumbsup:
